record.paper_title: Some open problems on excluding a uniform matroid
record.original_question: For every positive integer k, does there exist an integer n such that any binary matroid M with two n-interconnected minors M(K_n) and M(K_n)^* must contain a PG(k,2)-minor?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 9.5. For any positive integer k there is an integer n such that, if M is a binary matroid with two n-interconnected minors M(Kn) and M(Kn)∗, then M contains a PG(k, 2)-minor.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Work in the class of finite binary matroids (matroids representable over GF(2)). For a positive integer n, two minors N1 and N2 of a matroid M are said to be n-interconnected if M cannot be expressed as a 2-sum or related low-connectivity decomposition that separates N1 from N2 with separations of order less than n; more precisely, every separation of M of order less than n has both N1 and N2 entirely on one side. Let M(K_n) denote the cycle matroid of the complete graph K_n, and M(K_n)^* its dual. Let PG(k,2) denote the rank-(k+1) binary projective geometry.

Prove or disprove: for every positive integer k there exists an integer n = n(k) such that every binary matroid M which contains both M(K_n) and M(K_n)^* as n-interconnected minors must also contain PG(k,2) as a minor.
artifact.status_search_result: A targeted web search did not surface any resolution of this conjecture about binary matroids containing highly interconnected graphic and cographic minors forcing a projective-geometry minor. It is stated as a conjecture in the matroid-minors literature, and no published proof or disproof was located, so it appears still open.
